item.title: Inter star Francesco Pio Esposito sets incredible record as Italy’s most efficient goalscorer in history
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Inter sensation Francesco Pio Esposito has made Italian football history by recording the best goals-per-minute ratio ever seen for the national team. The young striker has surprisingly surpassed Azzurri legends like Luigi Riva and Silvio Piola with his prolific international strike rate. Setting a new Italian scoring record Esposito has officially written his name into the Italian football history books. The 21-year-old has established the best goals-per-minute ratio ever recorded for the Italy national team. The Inter striker has been in sensational form on the international stage, netting nine goals in just 14 appearances for his country. That includes his two goals during the Azzurri’s 3-1 comeback victory over France at the San Siro. That remarkable return equates to a phenomenal average of one goal every 88 minutes. This astonishing strike rate places the young forward at the very top of Italy's all-time efficiency charts. He has now comfortably outpaced several renowned figures who previously dominated the international scoring rankings. Surpassing former forward Enrico Chiesa To put Esposito's remarkable achievement into perspective, his ruthless finishing has seen him eclipse Enrico Chiesa in the record books. Chiesa previously held a highly respected benchmark, averaging a goal every 91 minutes. However, Chiesa only managed to score seven times during his entire international career with the Azzurri. Esposito has already bypassed that overall tally while maintaining a superior scoring frequency. The third-ranked player on this exclusive list is Julio Libonatti, a striker with dual Argentine-Italian citizenship. Libonatti, who represented Italy between 1926 and 1932, scored 15 goals in 17 games at a rate of one every 102 minutes. Bettering true Italian football legends Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Esposito's record is that he is currently outperforming Italy's greatest ever strikers. Luigi Riva, the all-time leading scorer in the history of the national side, sits further down the efficiency list. Riva famously netted 35 times for the Azzurri, a total unmatched by any other Italian player. Yet, his legendary strike rate stood at one goal every 106 minutes, firmly behind Esposito's current pace. Meanwhile, Silvio Piola, who ranks third on Italy's all-time top scorers list with 30 goals, averaged a strike every 103 minutes. What's next for Esposito? As a player with immense potential, Esposito will now focus on maintaining this historic momentum. The 21-year-old must now translate this ruthless international form into consistent club performances to secure a regular starting berth. item.title: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut
item.description: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut An assist against Manchester City, two against FC Augsburg and now a goal on his debut for the Germany senior national team . Brajan Gruda was named in the starting XI for Germany’s 3-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League, wearing the number ten shirt. Head coach Jürgen Klopp had already described the Leipzig attacker as a “street footballer, simply a brilliant player to watch” ahead of the match. Gruda with a solo run from his own half Operating on the right wing, Brajan repeatedly looked to take on his man against a Serbia side sitting deep. After around 20 minutes, he delivered a pinpoint cross onto the head of Kai Havertz. Shortly after the break, Gruda embarked on a solo run during a spell of Serbian pressure. Receiving a low pass from Joshua Kimmich, he turned away from his marker inside his own half . Approaching the penalty area, he left another defender trailing before slotting a low left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner . Nine successful dribbles on Germany debut - only Jamal Musiala has managed more Against Serbia, Brajan completed nine of his 14 attempted dribbles . According to Opta, only Jamal Musiala has recorded more successful dribbles in a single appearance for Germany over the past ten years. Musiala managed 13 against Costa Rica at the 2022 World Cup. “ It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling with the ball. I just do it . It just happens,” Brajan said of his goal. Klopp summed up the moment in his interview with RTL: “Brajan then calmly put an end to the opposition’s brief resurgence.” Klopp raves about Gruda’s feel for the game “What a debut,” said RTL commentator Wolff-Christoph Fuss as Brajan was substituted off in the 86th minute. Klopp was particularly impressed by the way Gruda switched between keeping things simple and taking on opponents with daring dribbles. “Brajan is an exceptional talent ; he has exceptional ability . The way he mixed things up today, playing simple passes before taking risks again – it was really lovely to watch .” Germany face the Netherlands on Monday evening. Asked whether he could feature in the starting XI again, Brajan replied: “Thankfully, I’ve come through it well. item.title: Kimi Antonelli meets Italian president Sergio Mattarella
item.description: Motorsport photo "To President Mattarella, with great admiration," signed Kimi Antonelli . The new Formula 1 world champion is in the middle of a whirlwind of meetings, events and celebrations for the world title he won two weeks ago at the Mexico Grand Prix, with which he ended a title drought for an Italian driver to win the world championship dating back to 1953. Antonelli, together with his parents Marco and Veronica and his sister Maggie, was received on Friday by the president of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella. The meeting took place at the Quirinale in Rome, with Antonelli giving the president one of his official helmets with a dedication written on the visor. Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Antonelli spoke with the highest office of the Italian state, explaining to him the sensations of wearing a helmet during a race, but also what driving a Formula 1 single-seater entails from a physical point of view. "You lose roughly a couple of kilograms," he said. "We have the fireproof suit, which is also hot. We train to be as ready as we can and to be able to withstand the heat we experience when we drive. But then after the session you jump into a tub of cold water..." The president then asked: "But was it like that in Formula 2 as well? And in karts?" "In karts a little less so," Antonelli replied. "You are much more out in the open. In a single-seater you are enclosed. But in F2 the races last a little less and are less physical. In Formula 1 the race lasts an average of an hour and a half. But will you come and see some races next year? Maybe at Monza? It would be very nice to have you with us." Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Mattarella, with a smile, replied: "I really hope so. Now Formula 1 attracts me a lot! The last time was several years ago. It is always complicated, because my movements are complex... But this new situation [referring to Antonelli's competitiveness] greatly encourages me." The meeting with the president was only the latest of Antonelli's engagements. A few hours earlier, Antonelli had attended the match between the Italian men's national football team and the French side, which Italy won 3-1, while the previous day he had stopped in San Marino - where he currently lives - to celebrate the world title. Antonelli will fly back to the United States, this time to Nevada, to contest the third-to-last round of the 2026 Formula 1 season in Las Vegas. item.title: Jurgen Klopp urges Germany to embrace "exceptional" quality after Nations League victory over Serbia
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-SRB-GER - AFP Jurgen Klopp has urged his Germany side to embrace their growing status as a European powerhouse following a dominant 3-1 victory over Serbia in the Nations League. The former Liverpool boss was full of praise for his team's tactical discipline and intensity as they moved a step closer to the quarter-finals. Klopp reflects on dominant display Germany took a significant step toward the Nations League quarter-finals on Thursday night, comfortably dispatching Serbia 3:1 on the road . Reflecting on the dominant display, Klopp insisted that his players must start recognising their own potential as they continue to evolve under his leadership. The result leaves Germany in a strong position in their group, shifting the focus to a high-stakes final fixture in Berlin. "The team played a really, really great game," Klopp told Sky Germany . "I think we have to get used to the fact that we are really good, that we can be really good. To be able to appreciate that correctly: of course we could score more goals today. But I just told the boys: 'I don't really care about that for the moment.' Because we can't say: 'We are starting processes and a development' - and then expect every time we look briefly: 'We must already be further ahead.' Even for ourselves, not just on the outside, for ourselves." Praises total control in hostile Serbia Klopp heaped praise on his side for navigating a hostile away environment unscathed, highlighting their composure as tensions boiled over. Despite facing a struggling Serbia outfit in a notoriously tricky fixture, the German tactician was delighted that his squad avoided any costly injury setbacks while dictating the tempo from start to finish. "It was outstandingly good in so many moments today, so difficult for Serbia, who are certainly not in their best moment. And yet you can really hurt yourself in such games - we didn't at all. So many sequences looked wonderful. In possession we had solutions, were dominant. The counter-pressing was outstanding. Intensity top. So, from my side, a really, really good game," the strategist added. item.title: “Are You Gonna Die?” – Alexander Zverev’s Unexpected Comment Toward Journalist Draws Priceless Reaction From Ben Shelton At ATP Finals
item.description: Alexander Zverev © Imagn images Alexander Zverev shared a hilarious moment with Ben Shelton and a reporter during the ATP Finals pre-tournament press conference. Zverev, Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar attended the press conference and a group photo on Friday evening. One journalist told Zverev that he had met all 30 World No. 1 players and that the German player was the last on his list. “I’ve met all 30 No. 1s in the world, and you’re the last one; you’re welcome,” the journalist said. Zverev instinctively responded with a joke, asking: “I’m the last one. Are you gonna die?” Zverev’s response left Shelton in splits; the American was seen hiding his face with his hand and giggling. The ATP Finals will be held from Nov. 15-22. Zverev will face debutant Jodar on the opening day of action at the Inalpi Arena in the afternoon session, followed by a Shelton–Fils clash in the evening. Alexander Zverev on being called the ATP Finals favorite Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz are the top two seeds at the ATP Finals in Turin. During the pre-tournament press conference for the John McEnroe Group, Zverev shared his view on being referred to as the tournament favorite, saying it is unfair. Zverev added that he is focusing on the challenge posed by Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar. “I think we shouldn’t disrespect anybody,” Zverev said. “I don’t think about Carlos right now. I think about these three young gentlemen because we have a very strong group and everybody shows that they know how to play tennis, otherwise they would not be here. item.title: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season
item.description: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande have emerged as the only four Real Madrid players to feature in every competitive match before the November international break, making them crucial to Jose Mourinho’s plans. The quartet have all appeared in Real Madrid’s 12 La Liga fixtures and four Champions League matches, but their minutes reveal a clear difference between regular involvement and workload. On that note, the likes of Mbappe and Bellingham have carried the heaviest responsibilities, while Cucurella and Diomande have contributed through a combination of starts and substitute appearances. Mbappe and Bellingham carry the heaviest workload Mbappe leads the group with 1,428 minutes and is the only one to have started all 16 matches. He has completed 12 of those 16 games, which shows just how central the French forward has become to Mourinho’s attacking plans. Bellingham, who is in sensational form this season , follows with 1,305 minutes and 15 starts, having also featured as a substitute on the one occasion he was not named in the starting line-up against Elche. Bellingham has started all but one game for Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Cucurella has accumulated 1,104 minutes through 11 starts and five appearances from the bench. Diomande, meanwhile, has played 891 minutes, starting nine matches and entering as a substitute in the other seven. Diomande makes an impact despite fewer minutes Diomande’s contribution in Europe is particularly notable, as he has recorded two assists and one goal in just 177 Champions League minutes, including a goal in Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Leipzig at the Bernabeu. In fact, during Vinicius’ absence, the former RB Leipzig star performed admirably, forcing Mourinho into a serious rethink once the Brazilian returns to La Liga action after the international break. Similarly, Cucurella’s involvement has also varied considerably. The defender played the entire Madrid derby against Atletico but was introduced only in the 89th minute against Rayo Vallecano. Cucurella’s time has been distributed as a starter and as a substitute. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) He has appeared in all four Champions League matches and provided an assist in the away fixture against AEK Athens. His minutes point to a player whose role can change according to the demands of individual matches. Courtois and Valverde narrowly miss the record Meanwhile, Thibaut Courtois and Federico Valverde are the two players closest to matching the quartet’s appearance record. Courtois has played 1,350 minutes across 15 matches, while Valverde has accumulated 1,181 minutes in the same number of appearances. Interestingly, both have spent more time on the pitch than Cucurella and Diomande, despite missing one of Madrid’s 16 fixtures.

item.title: Olivia Miles reflects on ‘special’ Year 1 with Minnesota Lynx in a heartwarming admission
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Olivia Miles has penned a message following an impressive debut season in the WNBA with the Minnesota Lynx. Miles was one of the top performers in the league and has cemented herself as one of the best rookies in history. She managed 790 points in 2026, which is a new rookie-season record, surpassing the previous total of 769 that was set by Indiana Fever ace Caitlin Clark in 2024. Miles also managed 239 assists for the Lynx in the most recent campaign. She failed to surpass record holder Clark in that area (337) but she still managed to secure the second-most assists of any rookie ever in the WNBA. Now, Miles has taken to Instagram to pen a message about her ‘special’ first year in the league. She wrote: “Finally had the time to realise what the f*** happened this year… “So grateful for the mems, the belief, the love. My circle continues to fuel me and Minnesota welcomed me with such open arms. “I learned a ton – to appreciate the triumphs and failures wholeheartedly. They provide meaning in all of this. But more importantly, to have unwavering faith in my vision. What a special way to spend year 1… can’t wait for the bee hive.” Miles’ Lynx finished first in the WNBA regular season but they failed to make the Finals on this occasion. They lost 2-0 to the New York Liberty in the first round of the playoffs, with Miles scoring 16 points across both games. item.description: Shohei Ohtani - LA Dodgers | © Imagn Shohei Ohtani has offered an honest assessment of his 2026 season, admitting he wasn’t entirely satisfied with his performance despite earning another top-three finish in the NL MVP race. His final pitching appearance of the season came on July 3 against the San Diego Padres. A recurring left knee issue, along with a right biceps injury, kept him off the mound for the rest of the season and eventually landed him on the 15-day injured list in September. Ohtani continued to play as a designated hitter but struggled to find his rhythm in the postseason, batting .192 with one home run and three RBIs across eight games. item.title: Taylor-Brown wins in Dubai to top T100 standings
item.description: Georgia Taylor-Brown has finished on the podium in all three of her T100 races this season, finishing first in Dubai and Pamplona and third in Vancouver [Getty Images] British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings. The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining. Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event. The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series , is aiming for her first T100 world title. Taylor-Brown won her first T100 race - which includes a 2km swim, 80km bike ride and 18km run - in Spain in May and was third in Vancouver, Canada in August. She hit the front in Dubai just under 4km into the run and opened a 30-second advantage before holding off New Zealand's Nicole van der Kaay to win by just 10 seconds, finishing in three hours 35 minutes and 19 seconds. Derron, who took the lead in the overall standings with victory in Vancouver, was third in Dubai, finishing two minutes seven seconds behind Taylor-Brown. Britain's Kate Waugh, the 2025 champion, was ninth, just ahead of team-mate Lizzie Rayner. Waugh missed the opening two events of the season with a calf injury and is eighth overall heading into next month's Grand Final in Doha.

item.title: Jimmy Connors Warns Ben Shelton and Juan Carlos Ferrero of One Major Challenge They Could Face: “Will He Listen?”
item.description: Ben Shelton. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect Tennis legend Jimmy Connors questioned whether Ben Shelton will take advice from Juan Carlos Ferrero, pointing to a potential challenge in their upcoming coaching partnership. Shelton has officially hired former World No. 1 and acclaimed coach Ferrero to join his team for the 2027 ATP Tour season. The news was announced in the first week of November. Unlike his previous full-time role with Carlos Alcaraz, he will work with the American part-time, attending about 12 tournaments each year. His schedule will prioritize Grand Slams, ATP Masters 1000 events, and the ATP Finals, allowing him to spend more time with his family. Ferrero will not replace Shelton’s father, Bryan Shelton. Instead, the two will work together as co-coaches, with Bryan continuing to lead practice sessions and travel with his son to tournaments that Ferrero does not attend. On the latest episode of his podcast, Connors discussed a potential challenge the coaching team could face, questioning whether Shelton would fully trust and listen to the experienced Spaniard. “There is one person who has already proven himself in this relationship, and it’s not Shelton. The question is: will he listen? That’s the problem. Ferrero has proven himself: he has raised Alcaraz to the rank of world number one, and he has already won several Grand Slam titles. He has an undeniable record,” said Connors. He added: “Now, if you recruit a guy like that, will you look at him out of the corner of your eye and ask him, ‘What do you have to bring me?’ Or ‘will you absorb everything like a sponge, take everything and try to trust him?’ It will be interesting.” Ben Shelton last played at the Paris Masters, where he suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Carlos Alcaraz in the final on November 8. item.title: Verstappen faster than everyone: promising figures for Las Vegas
item.description: Max Verstappen heads to Las Vegas with a second-place finish in Brazil under his belt, where low temperatures are once again expected. An analysis of race pace at Interlagos shows that Red Bull Racing was able to match McLaren and Mercedes in a range of conditions. One particular statistic from the dry phase offers hope for the Dutchman. Verstappen started the Brazilian Grand Prix from 21st on the grid and fought his way up to second place in changeable conditions. Teammate Isack Hadjar finished third, giving Red Bull its second double podium of the year. Conditions played an important role in the result. The race began on a wet track, after which the drivers switched to slicks. Rain returned in the closing stages. These different phases make it possible to compare Red Bull’s performance in wet and dry conditions. The pace on the soft tyres is particularly interesting ahead of Las Vegas, where qualifying and the race are expected to take place in temperatures of around ten degrees. Verstappen faster than McLaren on slicks in Brazil The gaps between Red Bull, McLaren and Mercedes were particularly small during the wet phases. The five fastest drivers on intermediates were separated by just over a tenth of a second. Norris recorded the lowest median lap time, but Hadjar and Verstappen were close behind. Hadjar, in particular, showed that he was comfortable in the changing conditions. Over the entire race on intermediates, the French-Algerian driver was slightly faster than Verstappen and even recorded the best median lap time among the drivers studied during the final spell of rain. The picture changed as the track dried out. Verstappen was the fastest of the eight drivers studied on the soft tyre, with a narrow advantage over Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli was also a few tenths off the pace. Hadjar dropped to fifth in this comparison, more than three tenths behind his teammate. The gaps are small, but they suggest that Verstappen’s performance during the dry phase was not solely down to his charge through the field in the rain. He also had enough pace on slicks to take the fight to the McLarens. One caveat is that tyre age and any delays or difficulties caused by traffic are not factored into the averages, as that data is unavailable. No signs of a major Red Bull disadvantage in tyre degradation The progression of the dry stints also offers some interesting insights. Verstappen completed his first 28 laps on the soft tyre before receiving a fresh set. His median lap time in the second stint was around 1.7 seconds lower. Hadjar gained almost a second and a half on new rubber, while Norris and Piastri also became significantly faster. These improvements cannot be attributed solely to tyre wear. The cars were lighter later in the race, and track conditions changed as well. It is, however, worth noting that these figures do not suggest an exceptionally large drop-off for Red Bull compared with McLaren. This is relevant to Verstappen’s prospects.

item.title: Suspensions over boys' team abusive messages claim
item.description: Some players at Kinsley Boys FC have been accused of sending racist and ableist messages [Getty Images] A boys' football club has suspended a number of players after allegations of racist and ableist abuse against a rival club. Claims of "deeply disturbing and hate-filled messages" being circulated on WhatsApp by members of Kinsley Boys FC followed a fixture with Route One Rovers FC in Bradford on 7 November. Kinsley Boys FC confirmed on Friday that a number of its players had been suspended pending the outcome an investigation. A spokesperson said the team was working with the Football Association (FA) and Northern Counties East Football League to ensure the matter was investigated "thoroughly, fairly and in accordance with the relevant regulations". "The club does not condone discrimination, abusive behaviour or conduct that falls below the standards expected of anyone representing Kinsley Boys FC. "We remain committed to ensuring that all individuals involved are treated fairly and that appropriate action is taken following the conclusion of the investigation," they said. A statement from Route One Rovers FC said it condemned the "vile racist, Islamophobic, discriminatory and abusive language" contained within messages reportedly shared in a Kinsley Boys FC players group chat. These included offensive comments directed towards a wheelchair user on the management team and Islamophobic comments about players, it said. A spokesperson from the club said: "This is not football banter. This is discrimination, and it is utterly unacceptable. "Such behaviour has absolutely no place in football or wider society." The club said it had also experienced racism last season and thanked the community for its support and solidarity. Kinsley Boys FC said it was co-operating with the relevant football authorities, including the FA and the Northern Counties East Football League. A spokesperson for the Northern Counties East Football League confirmed it had received a formal complaint concerning alleged discriminatory comments circulated via a private messaging group. "The allegations are extremely serious and include claims of racism, religious discrimination, disability discrimination and abusive conduct. "The matter has been formally recorded and referred to the appropriate authorities for investigation. The NCEL is committed to ensuring that football is inclusive, respectful and welcoming to all," they said. Football inclusion charity Kick it Out said it was "appalled" by the reports. "Discrimination has no place in football at any level, and we stand with everyone affected. "Our reporting team is aware of the incident and is working with the relevant authorities to ensure it is investigated and that those responsible are held accountable," a spokesperson said. item.title: Times Shield is an institution, says Amol Muzumdar
item.description: MUMBAI: India women’s cricket team head coach Amol Muzumdar urged young cricketers to respect the game, embrace failure and put the team first at the Times Cricket Shield prize distribution function at the MCA Lounge, Wankhede Stadium, on Friday. Recalling his early days in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar spoke about the advice he received from former India batter and 1983 World Cup winner Sandeep Patil when he made his Times Shield debut for Sungrace Mafatlal in 1993. The Times Award Shield was sponsored by The Times of India Cricket Shield’s celebration partner Heineken 0.0 (Mr. Vasant Bhandari) and Sterling Reserve Packaged Drinking Water. Incidentally, this is the 96th year of the Times Shield, which started in 1930. “Score 200. What’s the big deal about scoring 100? Everyone here scores hundreds. If you have the guts, score a double hundred, then I’ll accept it,” Patil had told him. The words motivated the then 18-year-old, but his debut innings ended at 97. “As I was walking back, the captain was sitting in front of me. He gave me a smirk. That was my baptism of fire in Mumbai cricket,” Muzumdar recalled. Three months later, he scored a then world-record 260 on his firstclass debut for Mumbai against Haryana in a Ranji Trophy pre-quarterfinal in Feb 1994. Muzumdar, who went on to captain Mumbai and score 11,167 runs in 171 first-class matches, offered three lessons to youngsters. “Respect the game. That is the most important thing. The game will respect you back multifold,” he said. He also urged players not to fear failure. “Failures are part of every cricketer’s life, it’s only a question of how you respond,” he said. Highlighting the importance of the Times Shield in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar said, “The Times Shield has been an integral part of Mumbai cricket. But I can tell you one thing: It was an absolute privilege to play in the Times Cricket Shield when I first started. It’s not just a tournament, but an institution. It is probably the livelihood of so many cricketers. It gave a platform, an encouragement to so many cricketers to display their talent. “It was just an honour to play in the Times Shield when I started and even when I finished in 2013.” Former India batter and BCCI Cricket Advisory Committee member Jatin Paranjape, the other chief guest, lauded the tournament’s role in strengthening Mumbai’s club cricket. For George Russell , the 2026 season delivered exactly that high-pressure scenario as Kimi Antonelli stormed to the world championship in the sister Mercedes W17. But rather than deflecting blame after a season marred by mechanical misfortune and driving errors, Russell is confronting the reality of Antonelli's raw speed head-on. Speaking on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show , Mercedes technical director James Allison provided a glimpse into the intra-team dynamic at Brackley, praising Russell for his brutal self-awareness in the face of defeat. "He does not hide from his own deficiencies. He's one of the most honest drivers I've ever had the good fortune to work with," Allison revealed. "He can see the areas where Kimi has been quicker than him this year, and he knows that those are things that he needs to bring to the table to compete on equal or better terms with this precocious young talent." Adapting to the new benchmark Antonelli's driving style - specifically his extreme use of mid-corner brake migration adjustments - allowed the Italian to preserve his rear tyres and extract blistering pace late in stints. Russell, whose strength traditionally lies in a more conventional, aggressive throttle application on corner exit, found himself outpaced in several tyre-degrading scenarios. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes But, according to Allison, Russell's willingness to acknowledge that specific technical gap is exactly what makes him a championship-calibre driver. "I do very much admire the fact that he looks straight down the barrel of that," Allison explained. "[We're] gonna see him looking to build the platform that is going to let him have a run at it next year alongside an amazingly talented team-mate." With the 2026 constructors' championship successfully secured for Mercedes, Russell's focus has completely shifted toward evolving his set-up parameters to match Antonelli's benchmark for the upcoming 2027 season.
